changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md`

- names `RecordDetailView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `51c294958` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1737 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2341 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36549643953)

### ① Derived judgments

1. RIGHT — the one code change. In `RecordDetailView.tsx` the header `sys_delete` `onClick` (already `async`) goes from `if (!window.confirm(msg)) return;` to `if (!(await confirmHandler(msg))) return;`. `confirmHandler` (line 703 at the head) is the page's own `useCallback` typed as the published `ConfirmationHandler` from `@object-ui/core`; it settles a Promise through `setConfirmState`, which the page renders into `ActionConfirmDialog` (line 2829, in the same return branch as the header, 2605 onward; the three early returns at 2360, 2364 and 2384 render neither header nor dialog). `ActionConfirmDialog` is the ONE component `useConsoleActionRuntime` renders too (import at its line 44, render at 780), and `ObjectView` hands that hook's `confirmHandler` to `useObjectActions` as `onConfirm` (ObjectView 1595-1601, 2252-2258) and renders `actionRuntime.dialogs` (3634). So the card's Expected — the same in-app dialog the list view uses — holds at the component: one dialog, two runtimes, a parity the 5835 pin already holds.
2. RIGHT — one argument, dialog defaults. The list view's delete reaches its handler through the runner (`useObjectActions.deleteRecord` then `execute`; `ActionRunner.ts` 1237-1240 calls `this.confirmHandler` with the evaluated `confirmText` and nothing else), so its dialog shows `actionConfirm.title`, `.confirm`, `.cancel`. The new caller passes one argument too, so the record page shows the same defaults. For precision: the two QUESTIONS are different keys with the same English today — the list view asks `objectActions.deleteConfirm` (through `recordDelete.confirmText`), the record page keeps its own `detail.deleteConfirmation` (en 1196). The PR body says exactly that (the page's existing `detail.deleteConfirmation`; title and buttons exactly what the list view shows) and claims no shared key. All four keys exist in `en` (1196 and 3129-3133); no pack key is added, so the claim's serial guard behind objectui#11039 is not engaged.
3. RIGHT — cancel and confirm. `ActionConfirmDialog.handleCancel` settles `false` on the Cancel button AND on Radix `onOpenChange(false)` (Escape, overlay), so no Promise dangles; the page's own `onOpenChange` only closes. Confirm settles `true` and the existing path runs unchanged: `dataSource.delete(objectName, pureRecordId)`, the `detail.deleted` toast, navigate to the object's list with `replace: true`. Nothing else on the page moves.
4. RIGHT — the two comment edits. Besides its declaration, `confirmHandler` has exactly two uses at the head (2535 the new caller, 2690 the `onConfirm` prop); the note above the declaration (686-691) and the parity test header (47-50) now say so, and both were false the moment the fix landed. Comment-only in the parity test, which is outside the claim's declared surface (③ 1).
5. RIGHT — the pin discriminates. `RecordDetailView.deleteConfirmDialog-11001.test.tsx` mounts the real page under a real `I18nProvider` (en) with the REAL `ActionConfirmDialog` (only orthogonal chrome is doubled: `ActionParamDialog`, `ActionResultDialog`, `FlowRunner`, `MetadataInspector`), installs a `window.confirm` spy that answers yes by property descriptor and hands the slot back after each test, opens the header overflow and chooses Delete by the `detail.delete` label read from the pack. Against the base code the yes-spy deletes at once with no `alertdialog`, so test 1 (`findByRole('alertdialog')`, question by key, default buttons by key, no delete, spy uncalled, path unchanged) is red there; the dev's ablation reads 3 failed with that reason. Tests 2 and 3 pin confirm (one `delete` call with the object and id, one success toast, router at `/crm_call`, which is what an empty `baseAppUrl` under a bare MemoryRouter yields) and cancel (dialog gone, no delete, no toast, path unchanged). Strings by key, not literals.
6. RIGHT — public surface. `@object-ui/app-shell` exports `.` and `./styles.css`; the diff moves no export, type, prop or schema, and `RecordDetailViewProps` is unchanged. The published behaviour that changes is which box one exported view asks its delete question in — a fix, not a widening of any accept set.
7. RIGHT — the seam chosen, against the triage direction. Triage said route it through the seam `useObjectActions` documents (`onConfirm`, falling back to `window.confirm`), as `ObjectView` does. The record page does not mount `useObjectActions`; it already owns a handler of the same published type feeding the same dialog, and the page's `ActionProvider` shadows the shell runtime for every action on it. Using that handler IS that seam with no second runtime mounted; mounting the hook here would have added the duplication the 5835 pin exists to contain. Within direction.
8. WRONG — none found.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11001-record-delete-confirm.md` declares `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. `@object-ui/app-shell` is published (`publishConfig.access: public`, 17.6.0) and a member of the `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json`; patch is the right level for a behaviour fix inside one exported view with no API movement. The body names the card, the change and that no pack key is added. Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Claim Re-read and Changeset Overwrite Report are all success on the head; the dev's report-only `check-changeset-claims` hit on `7997-detail-view-related-retired.md` is a mention of `RecordDetailView.tsx` in a paragraph about the retired `DetailView` mirror, which this diff does not touch.

Clause-②: no — matches the claim (5886653563, `Clause-②: no`) and the PR body. No type, schema or export moves; the diff is one call-site swap, two comments, one pin and one changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Dev flag — file surface +1, `RecordDetailView.confirmRuntimeParity-5835.test.tsx`, comment-only. Answered: the claim's surface named `RecordDetailView.tsx`, a pin and a changeset; the extra edit is three lines of header prose whose "nowhere else" sentence this fix made false. Leaving it false was the worse option; no assertion moved; the file runs green in the head's shards. Accepted.
2. Dev flag — local `vitest` narrowed from `packages/app-shell/src/views/` (565 files) to the 104 files naming `RecordDetailView`. Answered by the head's check-runs: the eight `Test (shard N/8)` runs and `Test (dist pins)` are the whole set, not a sample; all eight shards, the `Test` rollup and the dist pins concluded success on this head.
3. Dev flag — commit trailers are the model-free pair (`Claude-Session` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`). Verified on all four commits (0f12ede6, a537ec3e, 2a4a8095, 64c0db02). `AGENTS.md` 325-329 makes that pair the repo rule and says the harness attribution reminder yields to it. Answered; not a code concern.
4. `open_questions`: none declared — nothing to answer.
5. Out-of-scope finding (carrier: none; PR Acceptance notes): the record page's Delete does not go through the shared `recordDelete` core in `@object-ui/core` (objectui#10383) the list view binds to, so a package-owned `sys_permission_set` row (ADR-0094) would get the plain question and "Record deleted" here where the list view asks the reset question. Judged NOT this PR's to fix: the claim's surface is the confirm BOX on `RecordDetailView.tsx`; binding the page to `recordDelete` changes the question key, the toasts and adds a best-effort `findOne` lookup — the objectui#10383 family ("every host's list Delete"), a change with its own consent-copy semantics. An honest note, correctly not filed as this card's work. Does the PR make it worse: NO — before and after, the page asks `detail.deleteConfirmation`, calls the same `dataSource.delete` and toasts `detail.deleted`; only the box moved. Reach is unmeasured, as the dev says: `resolveRecordHeaderActionGates` gates Delete at the object level while the ADR-0094 flag is row-level (`managed_by`), so the page may well offer Delete on such a row. Escalated to the seat as a candidate card of its own; no blocker here.
